name: Bertie Frankel
desc:
Full Name: Bertie Frankel
Born: Early 20th century (exact date unknown)
Nationality: British / South African (sources vary)
Occupation/Role: Jewish refugee / traveller during WWII
Key Event: Fled Europe during Nazi persecution
Route (high level): Poland → Lithuania → Soviet Union → Japan → Shanghai
Critical Meeting: Received a life-saving transit visa from Chiune Sugihara in Kaunas
Reason for Fame: One of the refugees saved via the “Sugihara Route”
Significance: Example of humanitarian diplomacy and individual courage during the Holocaust
Survival: Escaped the Holocaust by traveling through Asia
Legacy: Remembered in Holocaust archives and exhibits about Sugihara’s actions

descByCountry.Poland: After Invasion of Poland in September 1939, Nazi occupation forced many Jewish families, including Bertie Frankel’s, to flee east
descByCountry.Lithuania: He received a transit visa from Sugihara, which allowed him to legally travel through the Soviet Union and Japan
descByCountry.Vladivostok: Refugees traveled on the Trans-Siberian Railway with their Japanese transit visas
descByCountry.Japan: Refugees stayed temporarily in Japan. Bertie, like others, awaited further travel arrangements to safer countries
descByCountry.China: When Japan tightened visa rules, most Jewish refugees (including Bertie) were sent to the Shanghai Ghetto
descByCountry.Israel: After the war ended, many Jewish survivors—including Bertie Frankel—immigrated to the Land of Israel, then under British rule
